{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.4,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R39"],
      "pins": ["R39.1", "R39.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R39 is valued '24k' in the netlist and SPICE deck, but its library description and MPN describe a 24Ω part (FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor').",
      "expected": "A value field consistent with the selected part. If the part is 24Ω, the value should read 24R. If 24k is intended, the part number and description should be a 24kΩ part.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R39\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(property (name \"MPN\") (value \"FRC0805J240TSD\"))"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R39 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If built as the MPN indicates, a 24Ω resistor across the ±rails would draw a large current and load the supplies. If built as valued, the BOM part is wrong and the bleed or balance resistor will not match the design.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["D6", "R67"],
      "pins": ["D6.2", "D6.4", "R67.2"],
      "nets": ["NET0137", "Net-(D6-K2)"],
      "observed": "D6 pin 4 (A2, anode) and R67 pin 2 both sit on NET0137, which is also the U10 Y output. R67 pin 1 goes to D6 pin 2 (K2). The LED2 anode and cathode therefore appear to be tied to the same driven node through R67.",
      "expected": "The LED2 anode and cathode should be on different nodes, with the current-limit resistor in series between the driver output and the cathode, or the anode on the driven rail.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D6\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R67\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"153\") (name \"Net-(D6-K2)\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "The second LED of the dual package is likely never lit, or it is driven incorrectly. This is an indicator/status function.",
      "confidence": 0.2
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["Q7", "U1"],
      "pins": ["Q7.2", "Q7.3", "U1.1", "U1.6"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "VBUS"],
      "observed": "The ideal-diode PFET Q7 has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on VBUS. The LTC4412 VIN (pin 1) is on VBUS and SENSE (pin 6) is on +5V.",
      "expected": "For the LTC4412 ideal-diode arrangement, the PFET source should be on the VIN supply and the drain on the SENSE/load node, so that the body diode blocks reverse current from the load.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q7\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q7\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, `U6`)"}
      ],
      "impact": "Reverse-current protection on the USB power path may not work as intended. The spec's own note already records that the USB power-path arrangement did not work.",
      "confidence": 0.15
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The strongest candidate is R39, whose value field (24k) contradicts its 24Ω part description and MPN. Two lower-confidence wiring and topology concerns are also listed, but the rest of the netlist appears consistent with the spec."
}

anomalies.observed: R39 is valued '24k' in the netlist and SPICE deck, but its library description and MPN describe a 24Ω part (FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor').
anomalies.expected: A value field consistent with the selected part. If the part is 24Ω, the value should read 24R. If 24k is intended, the part number and description should be a 24kΩ part.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If built as the MPN indicates, a 24Ω resistor across the ±rails would draw a large current and load the supplies. If built as valued, the BOM part is wrong and the bleed or balance resistor will not match the design.

anomalies.observed: D6 pin 4 (A2, anode) and R67 pin 2 both sit on NET0137, which is also the U10 Y output. R67 pin 1 goes to D6 pin 2 (K2). The LED2 anode and cathode therefore appear to be tied to the same driven node through R67.
anomalies.expected: The LED2 anode and cathode should be on different nodes, with the current-limit resistor in series between the driver output and the cathode, or the anode on the driven rail.
anomalies.impact: The second LED of the dual package is likely never lit, or it is driven incorrectly. This is an indicator/status function.

anomalies.observed: The ideal-diode PFET Q7 has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on VBUS. The LTC4412 VIN (pin 1) is on VBUS and SENSE (pin 6) is on +5V.
anomalies.expected: For the LTC4412 ideal-diode arrangement, the PFET source should be on the VIN supply and the drain on the SENSE/load node, so that the body diode blocks reverse current from the load.
anomalies.impact: Reverse-current protection on the USB power path may not work as intended. The spec's own note already records that the USB power-path arrangement did not work.

parsed.summary: The strongest candidate is R39, whose value field (24k) contradicts its 24Ω part description and MPN. Two lower-confidence wiring and topology concerns are also listed, but the rest of the netlist appears consistent with the spec.
